input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: § 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment on Customer with no reduction or termination right — the playbook walk-away position. It also contradicts § 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment) and § 7.1 (Fees limited to Order Form amounts; no minimum-use charges). Because the whole paragraph is the offending commitment and the no-minimum position is already stated in § 12.3, straight deletion is the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; no substitute wording is required. Fallback offered in the comment: a single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a shortfall penalty.

proposal.summary: Delete § 2.1 in full, removing the three-year USD 2M/year take-or-pay commitment.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept take-or-pay commitments, so we have deleted § 2.1 in its entirety rather than rewrite it; no replacement wording is needed because § 12.3 already records that we have made no minimum-volume commitment and § 7.1 limits Fees to amounts identified in an Order Form. If a commitment is essential to your pricing, our fallback is a single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice and trued up rather than penalised.
